name: Question 2
worked_solution:
We apply the distributive law 

$$
CB+CA=C(B+A).
$$

So, we calculate $B+A$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}B+A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -\sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -\sqrt{3} & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & \sqrt{2} \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =4{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}CB+CA & =C(B+A) \\  & =C\cdot 4{I}_{3} \\  & =4C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We apply the distributive law

CB+CA=C(B+A).

So, we calculate B+A first:

B+A=[2−3−211−2−3−25]+[232−13232−1]=[400040004]=4I3

Finally, we obtain

CB+CA=C(B+A)=C⋅4I3=4C=[404020404].
